title: An invitation ({inviter}, {accepter}, {refuser}, {remercier})
description: Léa turns sixteen on Saturday and invites her friends and neighbours. Learn to invite someone, say yes or no kindly, and thank them: {Je t'invite à mon anniversaire samedi.} {Merci, j'accepte avec plaisir.}
can_do: Invite someone to a party: {Je t'invite à mon anniversaire samedi.}
Accept an invitation: {Merci, j'accepte avec plaisir.}
Say no kindly and thank the person: {Je vous remercie, mais je ne peux pas venir.}
Say what happens as a result with {du coup}

vocabulary.note: a regular -er verb: {j'invite}, {tu invites}, {nous invitons}. The first sound is the nasal in {vin}, with no n heard.
vocabulary.example_fr: Je t'invite à mon anniversaire samedi.
vocabulary.example_en: I'm inviting you to my birthday on Saturday.

vocabulary.note: a regular -er verb: {j'accepte}. {J'accepte avec plaisir} is the warm way to say yes.
a regular -er verb. {refuser de} + a verb: {Noé refuse de manger sa salade.} To the person who invites you, say {je ne peux pas} rather than {je refuse}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Hugo accepte, mais Madame Garnier refuse.
vocabulary.example_en: Hugo accepts, but Mme Garnier says no.

vocabulary.note: the verb behind {merci}: {je te remercie}, {je vous remercie}. A regular -er verb; write the e you don't hear: {je remercie}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Je vous remercie, c'est très gentil.

vocabulary.note: spoken French: it starts the result of what you just said. In writing, use {donc}.
vocabulary.example_fr: Maya ne connaît personne ici. Du coup, Léa l'invite.
vocabulary.example_en: Maya doesn't know anyone here. So Léa invites her.

concepts.term: Saying yes or no to an invitation
concepts.definition: To say yes, thank the person and accept. To say no, thank them, say sorry and say you can't come. {Je refuse} to someone's face sounds cold.
concepts.example: {Merci, j'accepte avec plaisir !} (Thanks, I'd love to!) {Je te remercie, mais je ne peux pas venir.} (Thank you, but I can't come.)

items.text: Hugo ! Samedi, j'ai seize ans. Je t'___ à mon anniversaire !

mistakes.feedback: {invites} goes with {tu}. With {je}, an -er verb ends in -e: {je t'invite}.
After {je t'}, use the present: {je t'invite}.
